content.overview: If the articles so provide, active Members of a Producer Company may have special rights, and the company may issue appropriate instruments in respect of those rights. After Board approval, such instruments are transferable to another active Member. For this section, a “special right” is a right relating to supply of additional produce by the active Member or another right relating to the Member's produce that may be conferred by the Board.
content.glance: Section 378ZC permits article-based special rights for active Members, with related instruments transferable to another active Member after Board approval.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZC (Special user rights). Active Members may have special rights if the articles provide for them, and the Producer Company may issue appropriate instruments for those rights. Instruments issued under subsection (1) are transferable to another active Member only after Board approval. The Explanation defines a special right as a right relating to supply of additional produce by the active Member or another right relating to that Member's produce that may be conferred by the Board. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Special rights under the articles
sections.body: Active Members may, if so provided in the articles, have special rights, and the Producer Company may issue appropriate instruments in respect of those rights.

sections.heading: Transfer of instruments
sections.body: Instruments issued under subsection (1) are transferable to another active Member of the Producer Company after obtaining Board approval.

sections.heading: Meaning of special right
sections.body: For this section, a “special right” means a right relating to supply of additional produce by the active Member or another right relating to the Member's produce that may be conferred by the Board.

provisions.title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZC: Special user rights

examples.title: Checking an instrument for special rights
examples.body: Check whether the articles provide for the special right, whether it relates to additional supply or the Member's produce within the statutory definition, and whether Board approval was obtained before transfer to another active Member.

hypotheticals.question: An active Member seeks to transfer an instrument representing a special right to a non-active person. What does section 378ZC require?
hypotheticals.analysis: The section permits transfer of the instrument to another active Member after Board approval. Check both the recipient's active-Member status and prior Board approval; do not extend the statutory transfer route to a different recipient category without a separate legal basis.

distinctions.title: Special-right instrument and ordinary share transfer
distinctions.left: Section 378ZC addresses instruments issued in respect of special rights under the articles and their transfer to another active Member after Board approval.
distinctions.right: Section 378ZD separately addresses transferability of Members' shares and attendant rights.

rows.left: Board approval and transferee as another active Member

misconceptions.trap: Assuming special rights arise automatically for every active Member.
misconceptions.correction: The section conditions special rights on the articles providing for them.

misconceptions.trap: Treating a special right as any general corporate benefit.
misconceptions.correction: Use the section's produce-related definition and the Board-conferred right described in the Explanation.

misconceptions.trap: Transferring an instrument without Board approval or to a person who is not an active Member.
misconceptions.correction: The section's transfer rule requires Board approval and a transferee who is another active Member.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should s. 378ZC be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Check articles for special rights. II. Confirm active-Member status and Board approval for transfer. III. Conclude.
